kind: A float control and a spiking test at full size, and a screen by slope on the server's test bed: pools that divide by the summed activity as before but train with the gradient of the energy.
why: stream_loudness.json: in the trained Transformer and the trained stack alike the stream is dense and close to Gaussian, and its ratio of root mean square to mean absolute value barely moves from token to token, so a trained division by the mean absolute activity is a division by the root mean square times a constant the gains absorb. What the stack's pool costs the Transformer (0.0691, of which a division by the root mean square recovers 97%, energy_pool.json) therefore lies in how the pool trains. The gradient that a division by the mean absolute activity passes through its divisor is the stream's sign pattern; a division by the root mean square passes the stream itself. Both are blind to the stream's scale, but they take different directions out of the gradient that comes down. The control gpool (--transformer-norm gpool, this commit) computes exactly the pool and gives its divisor the root mean square's gradient, scaled to the mean absolute activity; --pool-energy-gradient (this commit) does the same to every pool of a stack's reads, cells and output, so the stack fires the same spikes and only learns differently. The spiking energy pool changed both what its pools hear (a quarter more on the trained stream) and how they train, and was 0.0040 behind at full size; this separates the two.

arms.fs-tf3-gpool (float control): sched/bin/full.sh transformer fs-tf3-gpool --transformer-norm gpool: every LayerNorm becomes the pool, trained through its divisor as a division by the root mean square; the parameters of fs-tf3-pool
arms.fs-loop6-lift-gr (full size): sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop6-lift-gr --lr 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --pool-energy-gradient: the lifted loop whose pools train with the energy's gradient; 34,810,900 parameters, as fs-loop6-lift
arms.gr (test bed): sched/bin/arm.sh stack --lr 1.2e-3 --seed 2000X [--steps 6000] --pool-energy-gradient: the delayed bed; 5,249,060 parameters, as the bed

base: Float: fs-tf3 1.305716 (LayerNorm), fs-tf3-pool 1.374858, fs-tf3-spool 1.307705. Full size: fs-loop6-lift 1.300729 (and fs-loop6-lift-en 1.304714). Test bed: bed24-lr12-s1 1.486381, bed24-lr12-s2 1.492556, rd-base-6k-s1 1.621562, rd-base-6k-s2 1.628309.
runs: fs-tf3-gpool, fs-loop6-lift-gr, gr-6k-s1, gr-6k-s2, gr-24k-s1, gr-24k-s2 on GPU 1 once fsp-lift's scoring is done in the window of 2026-11-26 (GPU 0 then holds fsp-lift2 alone), and whatever does not fit there in the weekend window; on a new code copy of the commit that records this, launch-checked on the server's CPU first: the float control first, then the full-size pilot, then the bed.
measure: The float control as full_size_layout_in_floats.json (windows of 496 bytes of history before 16 scored), paired with fs-tf3, fs-tf3-pool and fs-tf3-spool. The stack's runs by arm.sh's and full.sh's scores (eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights), paired with the base of each seed and length and split by context (near 240, far 8,192); the pulses a byte.
reading: Float: the gradient is the pool's price if fs-tf3-gpool costs at most a quarter of the pool's 0.0691 against fs-tf3 (0.0173 or less); if it still costs three quarters (0.0518 or more), the price lies elsewhere in how the pool trains (its early updates, while the stream may still be loud, or its learned rest), which the next diagnostic asks. Full size: pools that train with the energy's gradient join the next full-length run if fs-loop6-lift-gr is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6-lift with the paired interval clear of zero; between 0 and 0.005 better a second seed decides; worse, they stay off at full size whatever the bed shows. Test bed: the shared reading of experiments/read_lead_study.py (--arm gradient gr-24k-s1 gr-24k-s2 --arm-short gradient gr-6k-s1 gr-6k-s2 against bed24-lr12 and rd-base-6k): a fix, a constant gain or a fail; a mean lead of at least 0.005 after 24,000 updates with both seeds ahead adopts it on the bed. The stack's own readings decide for the stack; the float control says why.
seen_before_recording: energy_pool.json with its three results and stream_loudness.json with its result; tests/test_pool_gradient.py (the whole suite passes). No run with these pools or this control has trained.

result_float.checked: The run trained with --transformer-norm gpool (its results name the norm gpool) at fs-tf3's rate and length, 98,304,000 targets. Its score is within 0.00001 of fs-tf3-own's 1.297332; the two are different models (34,740,247 against 34,883,072 parameters, and their bits differ piece by piece with the spread of any other pair, 2.37 bits a piece of 16 bytes), so the agreement is chance.
result_float.reading: The gradient is the pool's price, all of it. The reading asked whether fs-tf3-gpool costs 0.0173 or less against fs-tf3; it costs nothing: the Transformer whose every norm is the stack's pool, dividing by the mean absolute activity and trained through its divisor as a division by the root mean square, is 0.0084 better than the Transformer with its LayerNorms [0.0075, 0.0092], where the same pool trained through its own divisor is 0.0691 worse. The 0.0775 between the two pools is how the divisor passes its gradient and nothing else: both compute the same division. The gain against LayerNorm is on new contexts (0.0086 on 76% of the bytes) and near copies (0.0161). Beside the reading: it is also 0.0104 better than the pool that divides by the root mean square itself, whose trained division differs from this one by a constant (stream_loudness.json); that is one seed against one seed, and the spread between two full-size float runs of one recipe has not been measured, so it is reported and not read. For the stack the float control only says why: the stack's own runs decide (fs-loop6-lift-gr at full size, gr-6k and gr-24k on the bed).
result_float.seen while reading: gr-24k-s1's score on the server, 1.48907 (bed24-lr12-s1: 1.486381); the bed's reading waits for its four runs and fs-loop6-lift-gr for its scoring.
